subject: Week 42: start the 12-month visit file — four things to write down
bodyText:
This week
Days 292 through 298 mark 11 months, the point where infant becomes toddler in the literal sense of the word. Receptive vocabulary is running roughly 50 to 100 words against an expressive count of zero to 10, and that gap is the normal shape of this month rather than a lag. Motor: cruising and furniture-walking for many (CDC checkpoint: 12 months) and three to 10 independent steps for some, with the walks-alone checkpoint at 15 months; socially, peekaboo is reliable and pat-a-cake is emerging on the 1-year checklist.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Separation distress at drop-off and a brief return of bedtime resistance — keep the handoff short and the routine identical, and it resolves on its own.
- [monitor] No babble, no joint attention, and no interest in shared games, all three at once — that combination belongs in front of the pediatrician; the absence of words alone does not.
- [monitor] A consistent one-sided preference when cruising or stepping, or a limp. Asymmetry is worth a look even though a slow overall pace is not.
- [call within 24h] Illness that persists past three days, or a fever that returns after a clear day.
- [call now] Severe respiratory distress, fever ≥102F rectal with lethargy, or blue lips or unresponsiveness — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Open the 12-month visit file and add to it daily: the running word list including approximations, the sleep pattern, the eating range, and where he stands on the motor checkpoints. Two months of notes beats recall in the exam room, and this visit carries five vaccines plus hemoglobin and lead screening. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/
- Close the baby-sign question before the practical window ends Mar 7 — free at home is the only version worth running, since the one longitudinal RCT found no language acceleration and a 17-study review supports no developmental claims. The ceiling is less frustration, not faster speech. Hanen Centre on baby sign evidence: https://www.hanen.org/information-tips/does-baby-sign-make-a-difference
- Play peekaboo and pat-a-cake on a fixed script — same words, same pauses, every time. Both sit on the CDC 1-year checklist, and the predictability is what lets him anticipate his turn and take it. CDC 1-year milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
- Cut the book rotation down to three titles and repeat them. Repetition is what converts a heard word into a mapped one at this stage, and he will start turning to the page he wants before he can name what is on it. Reach Out and Read: https://reachoutandread.org/

Upcoming
- Day 364-380 (May 10-26, 2027): 12-month well visit — MMR, varicella, hepatitis A, PCV #4 and the Hib booster, plus hemoglobin and lead screening. The booking call goes out in late March; the notes file starts this week.
- Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit due by the first birthday — the AAP dental home starts at age one, so book the spring appointment when you book the 12-month visit.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Plays peekaboo (initiates by covering and uncovering face)
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Active game initiation, not just smiling when you hide. Demonstrates object permanence in action.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/plays-peekaboo/complete

- Plays games like pat-a-cake
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Imitative gesture game. Joint attention + motor imitation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/plays-pat-a-cake/complete

- Waves bye-bye
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Intentional gesture with social meaning.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/waves-bye/complete

- Calls a parent 'mama' or 'dada' or another name
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Specifically referring to a person, not generalized babble. First true word for many babies.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calls-parent-by-name/complete

- Understands 'no' (pauses or stops when you say it)
  AAP window: day 270-365
  What to look for: Receptive language. Compliance is a much later milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/understands-no/complete
